grounding.claim: Role 'Map owner' may do everything 'Map reader' may do
grounding.note: The map records this only as an `includes` relation on R1 with `at: null, source: null` (dump --record R1), and it holds because the product has NO authorization at all: grepping serve.py for role/permission/authoriz/authentic/login finds only an OSError PermissionError catch. do_GET's only gates are the loopback Host check (line 634) and the project slug lookup, so serve.py:640 -- the entry point the map gives UC5, the Map reader's use case -- answers whoever runs the server, which is the Map owner. Nothing grants the privilege because nothing restricts it.

grounding.claim: Rule 'A served map is reachable only from the machine that runs the server.' is enforced at tools/coyomap/viewer/serve.py:885 — Opens the listening address on this machine alone, so a connection from another machine never arrives.
grounding.note: Line 885 is `httpd = ThreadingHTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", port), Handler)` -- the socket is bound to loopback, so a remote TCP connection never reaches the handler. I grepped tools/ for ThreadingHTTPServer/HTTPServer(/0.0.0.0 and this is the only bind in the product; there is no --host flag that could widen it.

grounding.claim: Rule 'A served map is reachable only from the machine that runs the server.' is enforced at tools/coyomap/viewer/serve.py:634 — Refuses a page request whose address names any host other than this machine.
grounding.note: Line 634 is `if not _loopback_host(self.headers.get("Host", "")):` -> 403 `host not allowed`, the first statement of do_GET so every GET route passes it. I read _loopback_host at 583-594: it strips an optional port or IPv6 brackets and requires membership of {127.0.0.1, localhost, ::1}; an absent Host returns True, which the docstring states is deliberate (not a browser rebinding vector).

grounding.claim: Rule 'A served map is reachable only from the machine that runs the server.' is enforced at tools/coyomap/viewer/serve.py:655 — Refuses the same way for a request that changes the remembered project list.
grounding.note: Line 655 repeats the same `_loopback_host` check as the first statement of do_POST, and do_POST (660-667) is the only route that mutates the remembered project list: api/open, api/forget and api/reorder. Same helper at 583-594, same 403.

grounding.claim: Rule 'A project folder is served only when it was deliberately added, never because the server found it.' is enforced at tools/coyomap/viewer/serve.py:883 — Builds the served set from the remembered folder list alone, with no search of the disk.
grounding.note: Line 883 is `Handler.projects = build_projects(store.list())`. I read build_projects (269-283): it iterates the folders it is handed and calls load_project on each; and RecentsStore.list (tools/coyomap/viewer/recents.py:88) just returns `list(self.folders)`. Neither one globs, walks or scandirs, so the served set is exactly the remembered list.

grounding.claim: Rule 'A project folder is served only when it was deliberately added, never because the server found it.' is enforced at tools/coyomap/viewer/serve.py:697 — Refuses to add a folder that holds no coyomap data folder inside it.
grounding.note: Line 697 is `if not _has_coyomap(p):` in _open -> 400 `that folder has no .coyomap/ folder`. _has_coyomap (104-111) tests `(folder / ".coyomap").is_dir()`. _open is reached only from do_POST, which has already applied the loopback check (655) and the X-Coyomap header check (658), so the folder is always one a person named in a request.

grounding.claim: Rule 'A project folder is served only when it was deliberately added, never because the server found it.' is enforced at tools/coyomap/viewer/serve.py:878 — Applies the same check to a folder named when the server is started.
grounding.note: Line 878 is `if _has_coyomap(folder):` in serve(), guarding `store.add(str(folder))` for each folder passed on the command line; the else branch at 880-881 prints `skipping ... -- no .coyomap/ folder` to stderr. Same _has_coyomap helper as the _open path.

grounding.claim: Rule 'A project folder is served only when it was deliberately added, never because the server found it.' is enforced at tools/coyomap/viewer/serve.py:658 — Refuses a change to the remembered list unless the request came from this server's own start page.
grounding.note: Line 658 is `if self.headers.get("X-Coyomap") != "serve":` -> 403, sitting above the open/forget/reorder dispatch at 661-666, so no mutation of the remembered list happens without it. Nuance worth recording: this is a CSRF guard -- it stops a cross-origin PAGE, whose fetch cannot set a custom header without a preflight the server never answers, but a non-browser client such as curl can set the header freely. Combined with the loopback check at 655 that still means only a local caller.

grounding.claim: Rule 'A request for a file can only ever reach inside the mapped project's own folder.' is enforced at tools/coyomap/viewer/serve.py:778 — Rejects a file request whose path is absolute or climbs above the project folder.
grounding.note: Line 778 is `if not _safe_rel(path):` -> 400 `bad path`, the first thing the api/src route does with the `path` query parameter. I read _safe_rel at 339-343: it rejects an empty path, a leading `/`, any backslash, a NUL byte, and any `..` path part. Both downstream readers (git_blob_size 314, git_show 333) re-apply it.

grounding.claim: Rule 'A request for a file can only ever reach inside the mapped project's own folder.' is enforced at tools/coyomap/viewer/serve.py:380 — Rejects a working copy read that escapes the project or names the version history folder.
grounding.note: Line 380 is `if not _safe_rel(path) or path.split("/", 1)[0] == ".git": return None` -- the first statement of worktree_read, which serves `api/src?at=WORKTREE` (called at line 784). _safe_rel (339-343) blocks an absolute path and any `..` component; the second half blocks a path whose first segment is the version-history folder.

grounding.claim: Rule 'A request for a file can only ever reach inside the mapped project's own folder.' is enforced at tools/coyomap/viewer/serve.py:387 — Refuses a file whose real location, after following a shortcut, sits outside the project folder.
grounding.note: Line 387 is `if not real.is_relative_to(real_root) or ".git" in real.relative_to(real_root).parts: return None`. `real` comes from `(root / path).resolve(strict=True)` two lines above, and resolve() follows symlinks, so a tracked symlink pointing outside the repo is caught here even though _safe_rel at 380 saw a clean relative path.

grounding.claim: Rule 'A request for a file can only ever reach inside the mapped project's own folder.' is enforced at tools/coyomap/viewer/serve.py:849 — Hands back a shared page asset only when the requested name is one of the two allowed names.
grounding.note: Lines 848-851 of _static: `ctype = _STATIC_FILES.get(name)` then line 849 `if ctype is None:` -> 404, and only past it does line 851 read `_FRONTEND_DIR / name`. I read _STATIC_FILES at 59-62 and it holds exactly two keys, `viewer.js` and `viewer.css`, so the claim's 'two allowed names' is literally right and no traversal string can reach the filesystem here.

grounding.claim: Rule 'A file that version history deliberately ignores is never handed back to the browser.' is enforced at tools/coyomap/viewer/serve.py:391 — Allows a working copy read when version history already tracks the file.
grounding.note: Line 391 is `code, _out = _git(root, ["ls-files", "--error-unmatch", "--", path])` in worktree_read. `--error-unmatch` makes git exit non-zero for an untracked path, so a zero exit means version history tracks the file and the read is allowed through to line 396.

grounding.claim: Rule 'A file that version history deliberately ignores is never handed back to the browser.' is enforced at tools/coyomap/viewer/serve.py:393 — Allows an untracked file only when no ignore rule covers it.
grounding.note: Line 393 is the fallback taken when line 391 said 'not tracked': `_git(root, ["ls-files", "--others", "--exclude-standard", "--", path])`, and line 394 returns None unless the path is actually in that output. `--others --exclude-standard` lists untracked files with the ignore rules applied, so a deliberately ignored secrets file is absent from the list and refused.

grounding.claim: Rule 'A version name arriving in a web address is refused unless it reads as an ordinary commit name.' is enforced at tools/coyomap/viewer/serve.py:790 — Refuses a requested version that is not a plain commit identifier.
grounding.note: Line 790 is `if not _valid_commit(at):` -> 400 `bad at= commit`, applied to the `at=` query parameter after the WORKTREE sentinel branch. _valid_commit (97-101) is `_SHA_RE.fullmatch(commit)` with `_SHA_RE = re.compile(r"[0-9a-fA-F]{7,64}")` at line 94, so only a bare hex SHA passes and nothing beginning with a dash can reach git's argv.

grounding.claim: Rule 'A version name arriving in a web address is refused unless it reads as an ordinary commit name.' is enforced at tools/coyomap/viewer/serve.py:366 — Refuses a branch or tag name that opens with a dash or carries unusual characters.
grounding.note: Line 366 is `if not _safe_ref(ref): return None` in resolve_ref. _safe_ref (353-357) requires a non-empty ref, `not ref.startswith("-")`, and a full match of `_REF_RE = re.compile(r"[0-9A-Za-z_./~^@{}+-]{1,200}")` at line 350 -- so a leading dash and any character outside that set are both refused before any git call.

grounding.claim: Rule 'A version name arriving in a web address is refused unless it reads as an ordinary commit name.' is enforced at tools/coyomap/viewer/serve.py:368 — Marks where the options end, so the name after it can never be read as one.
grounding.note: Line 368 is `_git(repo_root, ["rev-parse", "--verify", "--end-of-options", f"{ref}^{{commit}}"])`. `--end-of-options` is git's own marker after which every remaining argument is a revision, never a flag, so the user-supplied ref cannot be parsed as an option.

grounding.claim: Rule 'A version name arriving in a web address is refused unless it reads as an ordinary commit name.' is enforced at tools/coyomap/viewer/serve.py:301 — Skips the history read entirely when the map's own recorded commit is not plain.
grounding.note: Line 301 is `if not _valid_commit(commit): return []` at the top of git_ls_files, so the `ls-tree` subprocess on line 303 is never reached with a non-SHA. Its one caller is line 491, which passes `proj.commit` -- the commit recorded in the map -- so the claim's 'the map's own recorded commit' is the value being screened.

grounding.claim: Rule 'Code fetched from the public internet runs in the viewer only when its fingerprint matches the expected one.' is enforced at tools/coyomap/viewer/viewer.html:17 — Pins the expected fingerprint of the picture panning library.
grounding.note: Line 17 is `integrity="sha384-yc/c2Lk1s2V2ir1rxvjo8YyVD9PlOlYTqpNr3Wm1WIuAA30GlDYNx6U5104OiavY"` on the script tag opened at line 16, whose src is https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/svg-pan-zoom@3.6.1/dist/svg-pan-zoom.min.js -- the pan/zoom library for the diagrams. `crossorigin="anonymous"` on line 18 is present, which SRI needs to work.

grounding.claim: Rule 'Code fetched from the public internet runs in the viewer only when its fingerprint matches the expected one.' is enforced at tools/coyomap/viewer/viewer.html:20 — Pins the expected fingerprint of the diagram drawing library.
grounding.note: Line 20 is `integrity="sha384-yQ4mmBBT+vhTAwjFH0toJXNYJ6O4usWnt6EPIdWwrRvx2V/n5lXuDZQwQFeSFydF"` on the script tag opened at line 19, src https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/mermaid@11.15.0/dist/mermaid.min.js -- the diagram renderer -- with crossorigin anonymous on line 21. The comment at 13-15 says the self-contained UMD bundle is chosen precisely so SRI covers the whole library.

grounding.claim: Rule 'Code fetched from the public internet runs in the viewer only when its fingerprint matches the expected one.' is enforced at tools/coyomap/viewer/viewer.js:14094 — Pins the expected fingerprint of the styling that colours source code.
grounding.note: Line 14094 is `css.rel = 'stylesheet'; css.href = HLJS_CSS; css.integrity = HLJS_CSS_SRI; css.crossOrigin = 'anonymous';` inside ensureHljs, before the element is appended at 14095. HLJS_CSS (14085) is the highlight.js github.min.css theme on cdnjs and HLJS_CSS_SRI (14086) is its sha384 -- the stylesheet that colours source code.

grounding.claim: Rule 'Code fetched from the public internet runs in the viewer only when its fingerprint matches the expected one.' is enforced at tools/coyomap/viewer/viewer.js:14097 — Pins the expected fingerprint of the code colouring library itself.
grounding.note: Line 14097 is `s.src = HLJS_JS; s.integrity = HLJS_JS_SRI; s.crossOrigin = 'anonymous';` in the same ensureHljs function, appended at 14100. HLJS_JS (14083) is highlight.min.js 11.9.0 on cdnjs and HLJS_JS_SRI (14084) is its sha384. The onerror at 14099 falls back to un-highlighted text, so a rejected file degrades rather than running.

grounding.claim: Rule 'A source link may open only through an address belonging to a known code editor.' is enforced at tools/coyomap/viewer/viewer.js:14880 — Offers no link when the built address is not one a known editor answers.
grounding.note: Line 14880 is `return ALLOWED_OPEN_SCHEMES.has(uriScheme(uri)) ? uri : null;` -- the last statement of editorUri, applied to the FILLED template, not the raw one. ALLOWED_OPEN_SCHEMES (14811-14815) is a 23-name set of editor schemes only; its comment says it blocks javascript:/data:/file:/http(s):. I opened the one call site, doOpenSource at 14924-14925: a null return is not fired, and control falls through to the https GitHub blob URL at 14927, so the guard cannot be bypassed by its caller.

grounding.claim: Rule 'A source link may open only through an address belonging to a known code editor.' is enforced at tools/coyomap/viewer/viewer.js:15011 — Refuses to save a hand-typed link pattern whose address is not a known editor one.
grounding.note: Line 15011 is `if (!ALLOWED_OPEN_SCHEMES.has(uriScheme(custom))) {` inside saveSettings, and the block returns at 15013 before the lsSet writes at 15020, so a rejected template is never stored. It is reached only when the chosen target id is 'custom' (15009), which is the hand-typed case. Same 23-scheme set as line 14880.

grounding.claim: Rule 'A run refuses to read or overwrite coyomap's own map unless the operator declares coyomap is the project being mapped.' is enforced at tools/coyomap/model.py:1443 — Refuses to read a map stored inside coyomap's own copy unless the run declared that coyomap is the project.
grounding.note: Lines 1436-1448 of resolve_map_path: the path is resolved, and unless COYOMAP_SELF_MAP is 1/true/yes (1437) a `resolved.relative_to(COYOMAP_HOME / ".coyomap")` that SUCCEEDS raises WrongMapError at 1443. I also triggered it for real: running `coyomap dump --map .../coyomap/.coyomap/project-map.json` printed 'refusing to read ... that is the COYOMAP CLONE'S OWN map', and the same command with COYOMAP_SELF_MAP=1 succeeded. Callers are the read verbs -- finalize.py:154/782/815, audit_model.py:1689, assemble.py:183, context.py:196, anchor_drift.py:409, validate_model.py:6583, grounding.py:1572/1672, balance.py:271, model.py:1455.

grounding.claim: Rule 'A run refuses to read or overwrite coyomap's own map unless the operator declares coyomap is the project being mapped.' is enforced at tools/coyomap/model.py:1408 — Refuses the same target for a write, so a stray build cannot overwrite the accepted map of coyomap.
grounding.note: Lines 1401-1411 of guard_wrong_map: same COYOMAP_SELF_MAP escape (1402), same relative_to test (1405), and line 1408 raises WrongMapError worded 'refusing to WRITE'. Its call site is tools/coyomap/assemble.py:976, `guard_wrong_map(out_dir / "project-map.json")` -- assemble is the only verb that writes a map, so the write path is covered by the same rule as the read path.

grounding.claim: Rule 'A run refuses to read or overwrite coyomap's own map unless the operator declares coyomap is the project being mapped.' is enforced at method.md:1369 — Tells the build the refusal exists, and warns that a hand written script is not covered by the refusal.
grounding.note: Lines 1369-1371 read: '`coyomap` refuses to read the clone's own `.coyomap/` unless COYOMAP_SELF_MAP=1 is set, which catches the verbs -- but a bare `python3` heredoc is not a coyomap verb, so the rule still has to be obeyed rather than relied on.' That is exactly both halves of the claim: the refusal is stated to the build, and the hand-written-script gap is warned about.
